newsitem.title: UK: Yorkshire Water sets cash-for-shares deal.
newsitem.headline: Yorkshire Water sets cash-for-shares deal.

text.p: British water utility Yorkshire Water Plc said on Thursday it planned a capital reorganisation to reduce equity and return up to 10 percent of the company to shareholders as cash.

The company plans to divide each ordinary share into two new ordinary shares plus two B shares. It would then offer to buy back these B shares at their nominal value of 36 pence each. The company also plans to consolidate its shares into nine new ordinary shares for every 10 existing ordinary shares.

Yorkshire chairman Brandon Gough said in a statement that the company, which in the past has suffered from bad publicity as a result of water restrictions, had made substantial investment in securing water supply.

"The group now wishes to improve financial efficiency in a way which allows all shareholders to participate, and believes the proposed capital reorganisation is the most effective way of achieving this," he said.

The move will raise gearing at the company, which also said it intends to maintain growth in total cash dividend by six to eight percent annually after inflation until 2000, subject only to there being no material adverse change in the water industry's political and regulatory environment.

SBC Warburg, on behalf of Yorkshire Water, will offer to buy the new B shares free of dealing expenses. Under the plan, a shareholder with 100 ordinary shares who sold his new B shares would end up with 180 new ordinary shares and 72 pounds cash. A shareholders' meeting to vote on the plan is set for February 26, with trading in the new shares starting on March 3.
